name: Birth of Muhammad and Arabian Context
summary: Muhammad ibn Abdullah is born in Mecca around 570 CE into the Quraysh tribe. Mecca is a major Arabian trading city and religious sanctuary controlling pilgrimage routes. The Arabian Peninsula is divided among nomadic tribes, petty kingdoms, and Byzantine-Sassanid client states. The complex religious landscape includes Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and polytheistic Arab religions.

_quarry.structural_significance: The social context of 6th-century Arabia, tribal warfare, merchant capitalism, religious pluralism, shapes the specific character of Islamic revelation and its institutional forms.
